transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Kapoor (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Jared Lin (Spectra Head of AI), Maya Chen (Spectra Infra Lead), Omar Farouk (Spectra PM)

Auto-summary:
Quick scoping call to align POC success criteria, benchmark plan, integration approach (OpenAI-compatible endpoints + SDKs), and timeline. Customer wants a 4-week POC focusing on latency and cost per 1k tokens for an in-product assistant. Security and on-prem/private deployment options discussed; initial leaning toward Dedicated but want to validate via benchmarks.

Topics Covered:
- Success criteria: latency (p95), throughput (QPS), cost targets, quality baseline
- Workload sizing: token distributions, concurrent sessions, KV cache usage
- Benchmarks: sample inputs, metrics to capture, 2-day run plan
- Integration: SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, structured JSON output/schema
- Timeline and next steps for pilot

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Aisha: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intro 
- I m Aisha, AE at Redwood, and diego is our se. we re going to run through the poc scope and what success looks like.
[00:00:12] Jared: Hey, thanks Aisha. I m Jared, head of AI at Spectra. we re exploring options to power an embedded assistant inside our trading desk product. main concerns are latency and cost, and we have strict audit/compliance needs.
[00:00:25] Diego: great. quick confirm 
- is the primary integration going to use the OpenAI-compatible api shape or do you want our native sdk?
[00:00:33] Jared: preference is OpenAI-compatible endpoints for dev velocity, but we d like to evaluate SDKs if there s a clear perf win.
[00:00:40] Maya: and from infra side we care about VPC connectivity, SAML SSO, and key mgmt (KMS/HSM). Also token retention rules and logs for audits.
[00:00:52] Aisha: understood, we can provide SOC2 evidence and a security pack. for POC we usually run on Redwood Dedicated so you get predictable throughput and can pin versions, but we re open to hosted if you want faster time-to-value.
[00:01:09] Omar: whats the expected timeline? product would like to see a working integration and numbers within a month.
[00:01:16] Aisha: typical POC is 3-4 weeks: week 0 onboarding + environment, week 1-2 benchmarks, week 3 integration and validation, week 4 wrap + decision.
[00:01:27] Jared: good. success criteria 
- p95 latency under 200ms for short prompts, cost target around $X per 1k tokens (we ll fill in exact), and quality comparable to our current model baseline.
[00:01:40] Diego: ok noted. on the workload sizing 
- can you share expected QPS, average tokens per request, and peak concurrency? those will drive batching and kv cache configs.
[00:01:52] Maya: we re looking at roughly 30 qps baseline with peaks up to 120 during market open. average prompt size ~180 input tokens, output ~120 tokens, with many short prefix caches per user.
[00:02:07] Diego: perfect, that s helpful. for caching we ll recommend prefix/KV cache to hit the latency target while keeping cost down. with Dedicated we can tune batch windows and kernel selection.
[00:02:18] Jared: about function calling
- we need the assistant to call internal tools (ie trade lookup, risk check). how does Redwood support that?
[00:02:26] Diego: we support OpenAI-style function/tool calling; our runtime streams structured JSON outputs and can enforce schema. small warning: function-calling semantics may differ slightly between models; we ll document the exact behavior and test it in the benchmark.
[00:02:41] Aisha: also note we have an SDK that offers helpers for tool invocation and structured output parsing; the SDK can do automatic retries and tracing hooks for observability.
[00:02:52] Omar: would you recommend starting with the REST OpenAI-compatible endpoints or the SDK?
[00:02:57] Diego: for speed start with the OpenAI-compatible endpoint 
- minimal changes. if you need lower latency or better observability toggle to the native SDK. we ll include examples for both.
[00:03:07] Maya: any gotchas around streaming and partial structured outputs? we plan to render streaming responses in the UI and then parse final JSON for downstream tools.
[00:03:17] Diego: streaming is supported; partial chunks can be inconsistent with JSON, so best practice is to use the SDK's structured output helpers or to buffer until the closing token, we ll show pattern code.
[00:03:29] Jared: benchmarks 
- what metrics will you capture?
[00:03:33] Diego: latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens generated, cost per 1k tokens, throughput, error rates, memory/KV cache hit rate. we ll also export traces and raw request/response for debugging.
[00:03:44] Aisha: we propose a 2-day benchmark run on a representative sample 
- you provide ~2000 requests with realistic token lengths and function-calling cases; we run them across: hosted (for baseline), dedicated-config-1 (lower-latency kernels), and quantized variant (cost tradeoff).
[00:03:58] Maya: can you run with our private vpc option? we need to test network egress, and data controls.
[00:04:05] Diego: yes; for POC we can spin up a private deployment or an isolated dedicated pool with VPC peering. there s slightly more setup time (week 0), but we ve done this many times.
[00:04:14] Omar: what about telemetry 
- we need per-request token-level billing traces to run cost projections.
[00:04:19] Aisha: Redwood Console will give per-route token breakdowns and cost estimates; we can export CSV/JSON of traces.
[00:04:26] Jared: any limits on function calling rate? some endpoints might hit backend services frequently.
[00:04:30] Diego: function calls are just part of the response flow; external tool calls you ll handle. we can put rate-limits and recommend batching/aggregation to avoid hammering downstream services.
[00:04:41] Jared: on quality 
- we have an internal eval harness. we want to avoid regressions. can you support eval hooks?
[00:04:48] Diego: yes, we support eval sets and can run continuous quality checks; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and model variants when regressions show up. we ll include a simple eval pass in the benchmark.
[00:04:58] Maya: about security 
- SAML SSO and RBAC are must-haves; do you support KMS integration for key rotation?
[00:05:05] Aisha: yes to SSO and RBAC, and our Private option integrates with customer KMS/HSM for encryption at rest. we ll share the security datasheet and SOC2 docs.
[00:05:15] Omar: price ask 
- rough numbers for Dedicated monthly commit and for hourly hosted?
[00:05:20] Aisha: i ll share a tailored pricing sheet; for the POC we can offer a short-term trial credit and a benchmark pricing model.
[00:05:28] Jared: ok great. can we outline the success criteria now so we re all aligned?
[00:05:33] Aisha: sure 
- propose: 1) latency p95 < 200ms for typical short prompts, 2) sustained throughput of 100 qps with p95 under threshold, 3) cost per 1k tokens below your target (customer to confirm number), 4) function-calls reliably parsed into structured JSON schema with >95% correctness on eval set, 5) security/compliance posture acceptable (SOC2 + KMS).
[00:06:00] Jared: that looks right. we ll confirm exact dollar targets and quality thresholds.
[00:06:04] Diego: technical note: to hit <200ms p95 we ll likely recommend Dedicated with tuned batch windows and KV cache; if we need even lower, we can adjust kernel selection and sequence offloading.
[00:06:17] Maya: can you document the SDK examples for function calling and structured output?
[00:06:21] Diego: yes, i ll attach code snippets: OpenAI-compatible call example, native SDK example with streaming+structured helpers, and a small server-side adapter for deterministic function invocation.
[00:06:33] Omar: about the benchmarks 
- we want to run them against a model family comparable to gpt-4o or our current open models; do you have recommended model variants?
[00:06:41] Diego: we ll recommend a balanced variant for accuracy-latency tradeoffs, plus a quantized cost-saving variant. we ll include per-model perf profiles.
[00:06:50] Jared: any risk of mis-transcriptions here? (laughter)
[00:06:54] Aisha: yes, fair. (laughs)
[00:06:58] Maya: devops questions 
- during POC who will own the test infra? we prefer Redwood to run the benchmark but have our infra team give network support.
[00:07:06] Aisha: agreed 
- Redwood runs the benchmark, customer provides traces, sample payloads and whitelists IPs for peering.
[00:07:12] Diego: also need a short list of endpoints you ll call (chat/completions/embeddings if used), and any custom tool endpoints to simulate function calls.
[00:07:21] Jared: we ll provide 2000 synthetic requests plus 200 real anonymized sessions to validate caching behavior.
[00:07:29] Omar: timeline recap?
[00:07:31] Aisha: week 0 (now to 7/18): onboarding, infra, and security paperwork. week 1-2 (7/19-7/30): benchmark runs and initial reports. week 3 (8/2-8/8): integration, SDK work and function-calling validation. week 4 (8/9-8/15): final report and decision.
[00:07:52] Maya: that works. we ll need Diego to share benchmark harness and an example tokenized distribution.
[00:07:59] Diego: will do, i ll attach a template CSV and a script to replay requests.
[00:08:05] Jared: anything else?
[00:08:07] Aisha: i ll send pricing and security docs post-call; diego will prepare the benchmark plan; maya to share traces. we ll schedule kickoff for next thursday.
[00:08:16] Omar: sounds good.
[00:08:18] Aisha: thanks everyone, talk soon.

(end of captured transcript — timestamps are approximate, some words may be transcribed imperfectly)
